artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let D be a period matrix domain (a classifying space for polarized Hodge structures of a fixed type, realized as an open orbit G(ℝ)/V in its compact dual, where G is a ℚ-algebraic group of Hodge type and V is the compact isotropy of a reference Hodge structure). Let Γ ⊂ G(ℚ) be an arithmetic subgroup acting properly discontinuously on D, and form the analytic quotient D/Γ. For each rational boundary component F_j of D (in the sense of Hodge-theoretic boundary components stabilized by ℚ-parabolic subgroups), let Γ_j be the arithmetic subgroup of the stabilizer acting on F_j, and equip F_j/Γ_j with its natural topology.

Question: Does there exist a separated, locally compact topological space (D/Γ)* with all of the following properties?
(i) (D/Γ)* contains D/Γ as an open dense subset.
(ii) Set-theoretically, (D/Γ)* = (D/Γ) ⊔ ⨆_j (F_j/Γ_j), the union running over a chosen collection of rational boundary components, each F_j/Γ_j carrying its natural topology as a subspace of (D/Γ)*.
(iii) For every smooth algebraic family X → S of polarized algebraic manifolds whose associated period mapping Φ : S → D/Γ is horizontal and holomorphic, Φ extends continuously to a map Φ* : S* → (D/Γ)*, where S* is a suitable (e.g. smooth projective) completion of S.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Griffiths in the late 1960s, has been the subject of extensive work. Kato–Usui constructed partial compactifications Γ\D_Σ of period domain quotients using fans of nilpotent cones, achieving the desired extension property in classical (Hermitian symmetric) cases and conditionally in general (subject to existence of a "complete fan"). Watanabe gave a counterexample to the existence of a complete fan in non-classical cases, so a fully general Kato–Usui-type compactification with continuous extension for arbitrary horizontal period maps is not known. More recent work (Bakker–Brunebarbe–Tsimerman, Green–Griffiths–Laza–Robles, et al.) has constructed Hodge-theoretic and toroidal-type completions of period maps in various settings (e.g., every two-parameter horizontal period map admits a log-manifold completion), giving partial answers. The general question remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the generalized toroidal completion of period mappings
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Kato–Usui partial compactifications and the conjectural complete fan; describes recent completions of period maps.
status_evidence.claim: General Kato–Usui-type completion with horizontal extension is conjectural and remains partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Completion of two-parameter period maps by nilpotent orbits
status_evidence.snippet: Every two-parameter period map admits a Kato–Nakayama–Usui completion to a morphism of log manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist (e.g., two-parameter case); general case still open.

status_evidence.title: Extension of period maps by polyhedral fans
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs extensions of period maps using fans of nilpotent cones, generalizing Kato–Usui.
status_evidence.claim: Partial compactifications giving continuous extensions of horizontal period maps are achieved under fan-existence hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Hodge Theoretic Compactification of Period Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Griffiths conjectured an analogue of Satake–Baily–Borel compactifications for period domain quotients.
status_evidence.claim: The problem originates as a Griffiths conjecture and motivates ongoing research.
